notes.title: Chapter map: Media & transport

headings.text: 🌳 Decide: which channel for this data?

notes.html:
How audio and everything around it gets between the person and the agent: the browser's capture, LiveKit's room model, the token that lets someone in and brings the agent along, and the side channels for captions, state and actions. The wire itself (WebRTC, ICE, TURN, SFU topologies) is owned by the networking pillar.

Where this sits

capture → carry → clean → detect → transcribe → endpoint → think → speak → yield → observe

Reading order

# Note Tier Stage You'll understand
1 Browser capture SUPPORTING capture constraints, the lobby, autoplay
2 Rooms, participants, tracks CORE carry the call as LiveKit models it
3 Tokens, grants, dispatch SUPPORTING carry the signed token that brings the agent
4 Side channels SUPPORTING carry captions, state, RPC
– Telephony and SIP BREADTH carry phone callers in a room
→ 010 WebRTC, SFU, ICE/TURN for voice pointer carry WebRTC for voice AI · WebRTC vs WebSocket · ICE, STUN, TURN · SFU topologies

Owners

Concept Home
Capture constraints, lobby, devices browser capture
Room, participant, track, SFU forwarding rooms, participants, tracks
JWT grants, token and API dispatch, metadata tokens and dispatch
Text streams, attributes, RPC side channels
WebRTC, ICE, TURN, Opus over RTP the networking pillar (pointer above)
Sample rates, frames, codecs audio for engineers

Decide: which channel for this data?

Ask in order If yes → Because
1. Is it audio or video? a track through the SFU jitter buffers, loss handling, NAT traversal
2. Is it text that streams (captions)? a text stream ordered, chunked, synced to speech
3. Is it small state the UI shows? participant attributes everyone sees the latest value
4. Is it a request that needs a reply? RPC request-response with errors

🔊 Our system in one table

What Status
Browser capture with AEC, NS, AGC, mono; lobby with meter and test tone
LiveKit Cloud room, 2 audio tracks per interview
30-min room-scoped token with explicit dispatch and metadata
Captions on lk.transcription, state attributes, pause RPC
Telephony not used

Game Day

Q11 WebRTC or WebSocket · Q12 call setup · Q13 TURN cost · Q28 channels · Q29 token, room, dispatch

notes.title: Browser Capture — Microphone, Devices, Permissions
notes.html:
References

W3C — Media Capture and Streams · ~/Projects/convo_client/src/lib/audio.ts, lib/devices.ts, components/DeviceCheck.tsx · ~/Projects/tech_documentation/ADR/voice_pipeline/as_built.md §2 row 1

TL;DR

The browser asks for the microphone with getUserMedia and a set of constraints (echo cancellation, noise suppression, gain control, mono). Do it in a lobby before the call: pick devices, show a mic meter, play a test sound, and catch permission and autoplay problems while they're cheap to fix.

Stage: capture → carry → clean → detect → transcribe → endpoint → think → speak → yield → observe · per session

Flow: lobby ─getUserMedia(constraints)permissionpick mic and speakermeter + test tonejoin the room with those devices

Recall

Prompt Answer
The four capture constraints we set echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, autoGainControl, channelCount: 1
Why a lobby permission, device choice and echo convergence before the first question
Autoplay browsers may block audio until a user gesture; the agent is silent until then
Why mono speech gains nothing from stereo; half the encode work
Draw the lobby's checks in order permission → device pick → meter → tone → join

The idea

Without it: the first question goes to a blocked speaker, the wrong mic, or a permission prompt the person hasn't seen.

It does: moves every device failure before the call, where it costs a click, not an interview.

It costs: one more screen before the call.

How it works

Check Catches
Permission prompt denied or dismissed mic access
Device picker the headset vs the laptop mic
Level meter (WebAudio AnalyserNode) muted or wrong mic
Test tone speaker choice, autoplay, and AEC convergence
Network estimate round trip to the server

Knobs

Knob Our value Trade
Capture constraints all four on off only for raw-audio needs
Camera local preview only, never sent privacy vs a video interview

🔊 In our system

What Value Status Why / source
Constraints AEC, NS, AGC on, mono lib/audio.ts
Lobby camera, mic and speaker pickers, mic meter, network pill; camera never sent as_built row 1, App.tsx
Robustness cases mic muted (V-41), autoplay blocked (V-42) written, not logged voice_interview_cases.md

Measure it

  • Metric — share of sessions failing in the lobby, by reason (permission, no audio, autoplay).
  • See it — client logs; the lobby's device and network pills.
  • Bounded by — the lobby itself: nobody enters a call without a working mic.

Pitfalls

Skipping the lobby to save a click

  • Why it's tempting: faster start.
  • Why it's wrong: device and autoplay failures then happen mid-question, with an agent talking to nobody.
  • Think instead: a short lobby that also warms up echo cancellation.

Connections

capture → carry → … — the first stage.

  • feeds echo cancellation its constraints.
  • formats explained in audio for engineers.

notes.title: Rooms, Participants and Tracks — A Call as LiveKit Models It
notes.html:
References

LiveKit — Rooms, participants and tracks (read 16 Oct 2026) · SFU topologies (networking) · ~/Projects/tech_documentation/ADR/media_transport/livekit_decision.md

TL;DR

A room is the call. Everyone in it is a participant: the person, the AI agent, a phone caller, a recorder. Each participant publishes tracks (mic audio, camera, data) and subscribes to others' tracks. The SFU forwards packets between them without decoding. The agent is just another participant, which is why the same model covers browsers, phones and recordings.

Stage: capture → carry → clean → detect → transcribe → endpoint → think → speak → yield → observe · per session

Flow: person joins roomSFUagent subscribes ─agent publishes voice trackSFUperson subscribes

Recall

Prompt Answer
Room the virtual space where the call happens; unique name, settings like max participants and empty timeout
Participant anyone or anything connected: user, agent, SIP caller, service
Track one stream of audio, video or data published by a participant
What the SFU does with audio forwards it; no decoding or mixing
How many audio tracks per call here 2 (person's mic, agent's voice)
Draw a room with the person, the agent and a recorder each box publishes and subscribes; arrows through the SFU

The idea

Without it: a custom WebSocket protocol per client type, your own jitter buffers, your own reconnect logic.

It does: gives one model (room, participant, track) for every kind of endpoint, with WebRTC underneath.

It costs: a media server to run or pay for, and a token for every participant.

How it works

Concept In our call
Room one per interview
Participants the candidate (browser) and the agent (job process)
Tracks candidate mic (Opus); agent TTS (Opus)
Data transcripts and state on side channels, not media tracks (side channels)
Events webhooks for room and participant changes, to the control plane

Knobs

Knob Trade
Empty-room timeout resources freed vs reconnect window
Max participants stops a third person joining an interview
Auto-subscribe simple vs bandwidth for many-party rooms

🔊 In our system

What Value Status Why / source
Media LiveKit Cloud SFU as_built row 2
Design self-hosted LiveKit, multi-node with Redis at scale livekit_decision
Webhooks room and participant events to FastAPI runtime_topology

Measure it

  • Metric — join time, reconnects, packet loss, jitter per participant.
  • See it — WebRTC stats in the client ("Join with internals"); LiveKit's dashboard.
  • Bounded by — LiveKit's reconnect and ICE restart; the agent keeps state across a reconnect.

Pitfalls

Streaming audio to the agent over your own WebSocket

  • Why it's tempting: simpler to start than WebRTC.
  • Why it's wrong: TCP head-of-line blocking, no jitter buffer, no NAT traversal, no echo cancellation path for browsers.
  • Think instead: WebRTC through an SFU; see the networking comparison.

Connections

capture → carry → clean → … — the media model.

  • wire details in WebRTC for voice AI, ICE, STUN, TURN, WebRTC vs WebSocket.
  • joined via tokens and dispatch.
  • the agent participant is a job.
  • Say it: Q11 · Q12

notes.title: Tokens, Grants and Agent Dispatch
notes.html:
References

LiveKit — Agent dispatch (read 16 Oct 2026) · ~/Projects/convo_agentic/meghdootam/dispatch.py · ~/Projects/tech_documentation/ADR/runtime_topology.md

TL;DR

Every participant joins with a signed access token (a JWT) that names the room and grants what it may do. The token can also carry an agent dispatch: "send agent X into this room, with this metadata". That way the agent arrives with the person, already knowing who they are and what the call is for.

Stage: capture → carry → clean → detect → transcribe → endpoint → think → speak → yield → observe · per session

Flow: browsercontrol plane ─signs JWT: room + grants + RoomAgentDispatch(metadata)browser joinsLiveKit creates room, dispatches agentctx.job.metadata

Recall

Prompt Answer
Who signs the token your control plane, with the LiveKit API secret
What's in it identity, room, grants (publish, subscribe, data), expiry, optional dispatch
Token dispatch vs API dispatch on first join of a new room vs any time from the server
Metadata limit 512 KiB, ideally JSON
Why the agent can trust the metadata it's signed into the token
Draw the token's fields identity, room, grants, ttl, RoomConfiguration.agents[]

The idea

Without it: the agent joins rooms blind and asks a database who the caller is, or joins before the person and greets an empty room.

It does: bundles authorisation and routing into one signed object the person carries.

It costs: token dispatch works only when the room is created; for rooms that already exist, use the API.

How it works

Dispatch Use
Automatic (no agent_name) prototypes only: every room, no metadata
Token (RoomAgentDispatch in RoomConfiguration.agents) user-started sessions
API (CreateDispatch) server-controlled timing; creates the room if needed
SIP dispatch rules inbound phone calls

Knobs

Knob Our value Trade
Token lifetime 30 minutes shorter limits a leak; must cover joining
Room scope one room –
Metadata candidate, plan, resume point more context vs token size

🔊 In our system

What Value Status Why / source
Token 30-min, room-scoped, with explicit dispatch to meghdootam as_built row 2, dispatch.py
Metadata candidate_id, plan_id, continue_from dispatch.py JobMeta
Why token dispatch agent never arrives before the candidate; no pre-created room whose dispatch can be missed dispatch.py

Measure it

  • Metric — token-to-agent-joined time; failed joins by reason (expired, wrong room).
  • See it — the agent's first log line with ctx.job.metadata.
  • Bounded by — short expiry and room scope.

Pitfalls

Putting trust-relevant data in unsigned client messages

  • Why it's tempting: the client already knows the plan.
  • Why it's wrong: the client can change it.
  • Think instead: sign it into the token's dispatch metadata.

Connections

… → carry → … — how a call starts.

  • minted by the control plane.
  • dispatches an agent job.
  • Say it: Q29

notes.title: Side Channels — Transcripts, State and RPC Beside the Audio
notes.html:
References

LiveKit — Text and transcriptions (read 16 Oct 2026) · ~/Projects/convo_client/src/sdk/SdkRoom.tsx · 02-Game-Day/meta_prompts/voice_realtime_model_answer_prompt_v1.md §7.2

TL;DR

Audio isn't the only thing between the agent and the screen. Live captions travel as text streams (lk.transcription), synced to the agent's speech; agent state ("evaluating", "paused") as participant attributes; and actions like "pause the interview" as RPC calls. Keep each kind of data on the channel built for it.

Stage: capture → carry → clean → detect → transcribe → endpoint → think → speak → yield → observe · per turn

Flow: agent speakstext stream lk.transcription (word-synced)captions · agent sets attributeUI state · client performRpc("pause")agent handler

Recall

Prompt Answer
Captions channel text stream topic lk.transcription
Interim vs final caption lk.transcription_final false/true; same lk.segment_id
Agent captions when interrupted truncated to what was played
User text into the agent topic lk.chat; interrupts and gets a reply
Request-response from client to agent RPC (performRpc, a registered method)
Draw the three side channels between client and agent text stream, attributes, RPC

The idea

Without it: state is guessed from audio, or squeezed into one ad-hoc data message format.

It does: uses the right primitive for each: streams for text, attributes for state, RPC for actions.

It costs: a small contract between client and agent repos (topic names, attribute keys, RPC methods).

How it works

Channel Carries Ours
Text stream lk.transcription agent and user transcripts, synced to playback live captions
Participant attributes small state the UI reacts to interview.phase (evaluating, paused, feedback_ready), interview.hint (cant_hear)
RPC client → agent requests with a reply pause the interview (PAUSE_RPC)
Text input lk.chat typed messages to the agent – (text fallback )

Knobs

Knob Default Trade
sync_transcription on word-synced captions vs text as soon as available
TTS-aligned timestamps off start/end times per chunk

🔊 In our system

What Value Status Why / source
Captions registerTextStreamHandler('lk.transcription') in the client SdkRoom.tsx
State participant attributes interview.phase, interview.hint fact sheet §7.2
Pause RPC from the client to the agent SdkRoom.tsx

Measure it

  • Metric — caption lag behind audio; RPC failures.
  • See it — the client's event log ("Join with internals").
  • Bounded by — captions truncated on interruption, so the screen never shows unsaid words.

Pitfalls

Showing interim captions as final

  • Why it's tempting: they arrive first.
  • Why it's wrong: they're rewritten; the screen flickers or shows words the person didn't say.
  • Think instead: replace interim with final by lk.segment_id.

Connections

… → carry → … — everything that isn't audio.

  • travels in the room.
  • captions come from streaming STT and the agent's speech.
  • Say it: Q28
